summary: px8my abuses npm/jsDelivr as a CDN to redirect embedding sites to a rotating author-controlled domain
details: The package's main script (px.js) injects a fullscreen loading overlay via document.write and an iframe pointing at a hardcoded external URL (https://mfmz.tjyhwy3.cn/H.html?c=0gjr). Any page that loads px8my — typically via jsDelivr's npm CDN path /npm/px8my/px.js — redirects its visitors into that destination. The tarball also ships update_px8my.sh, a maintainer script that rewrites the mfmz.* redirect host in px.js, bumps the patch version, runs `npm publish`, and calls purge.jsdelivr.net to flush the CDN cache, indicating the destination is intentionally rotated to evade domain blocking. The package provides no legitimate library functionality; its documented behavior is the redirect itself, sending caller traffic to a destination the caller did not configure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
